summary.intent: Run the GSD secure-phase workflow for Phase 44 (ipns-conflict-handling) to verify threat mitigations across 7 sub-plans and produce a phase-scoped SECURITY.md audit document.
summary.outcome: All 19 mitigate-disposition threats were verified CLOSED by the security auditor with file:line evidence, 7 accepted risks acknowledged, and a phase-scoped SECURITY.md written to `.planning/phases/44-ipns-conflict-handling/44-SECURITY.md`. The project's root SECURITY.md (inadvertently modified by the auditor subagent) was restored to HEAD before committing.

repo: The repo root SECURITY.md is a tracked GitHub security disclosure policy (supported versions, vulnerability reporting, security model) — not a phase audit log. It must not be overwritten or appended to by tooling.

Phase 44 spans 7 sub-plans with 26 threat entries across merge.ts, errors.ts, folder update/publish, file updateFileMetadata, shared-write, web file ops, return contract, and prunedCids filter components.
All 7 Phase 44 PLANs carried formal <threat_model> blocks, making register_authored_at_plan_time: true and enabling short-circuit if threats_open were 0 at classification time.
GSD commits use 1Password SSH signing — the gsd_run query commit helper must be run unsandboxed for signing to work.

code.finding: Newly created phase-scoped security audit document; correct output path per workflow is <PHASE_DIR>/<PADDED_PHASE>-SECURITY.md, not the repo root.
Original project Security Policy ends at line 73; auditor subagent appended 50 lines of phase audit content starting at line 74 — purely additive, recoverable via git checkout.

workflow: The gsd-security-auditor subagent wrote its output to the repo-root SECURITY.md instead of the phase-scoped path — the orchestrator must validate the output file location after the subagent returns, not assume it wrote to the correct path.
When a subagent modifies an unintended file, checking `git diff --stat HEAD` immediately after it returns is the fastest way to detect the wrong-path write before proceeding.

The GSD workflow short-circuit (threats_open: 0 AND register_authored_at_plan_time: true → skip to Step 6) only applies after classification; threats classified as 'mitigate' with no code verification yet count as open and must go through the auditor.

friction: The gsd-security-auditor subagent wrote the phase audit output to the repo-root SECURITY.md instead of the workflow-specified phase-scoped path, requiring manual detection, inspection, root file restoration via git checkout, and a separate Write to the correct path.

No guardrail in the auditor prompt or workflow prevented the subagent from targeting the wrong output file — the constraint 'Never modify implementation files' did not cover non-implementation tracked files like the project Security Policy.
open_items: The auditor subagent prompt should be hardened to explicitly specify the output file path and prohibit writing to any file outside the phase directory — currently only implementation files are protected.
Consider adding a post-subagent validation step to the secure-phase workflow that checks git diff for unexpected file modifications before proceeding to Step 6.
